bullets.text: /challenge's own charter already names the same gap /intent's did — 'endpoint into cc-learning-store; interim by-hand' — so the migration is closing a hole the component documented against itself, not one imposed on it from outside.

The template claim is currently pinned by a tooth that fires two FIXTURE tenants and asserts the seam's source bytes are identical across them. That is a real tooth and it is still a fixture; /challenge is the first tenant with a charter nobody wrote for the test, which is the only version of the claim worth believing.

Sequencing risk worth Akien's eye: child c is chartered as 'the remaining roster in one campaign' (eight skills). Doing /challenge alone first, and re-reading the template claim before the other seven, is a deliberate narrowing of that scope — cheap if the pattern holds, and much cheaper than seven copies of a mistake if it does not.

bullets.text: The Haiku spec is not a new project: its checklist reproduces I-the-system-is-a-learning-block's own corpus almost item for item, so the conversation was that intention's 'sorting out how' — this intent is its first code step, and berthing it anywhere else would mint the second vocabulary the merge of 2026-08-02 already killed once.

Haiku — the smallest model — did coherent design work when fed one bounded question per turn with Akien carrying the state between turns. That is a live measurement of the block shape working: the engine exists to give every block that property WITHOUT Akien being the carrier. The same measurement explains the Opus spiral: the model tier a session needs is a function of how much untracked state it must bind, which is exactly what the state log removes.

The existing learning_block is the SHELL (door/trace/finding/verdict/dial); the delta is the INNER loops plus infer:compile plus proof:validate. The TRACE organ already consumer-types 'training' at write — the compile corpus has been accumulating by design with no reader. infer:compile is that reader.

Distinction recorded, not a conflict: learning_block's dial measures verdict fractions (match rate at Akien's gate); proof:validate measures compiled-vs-model agreement and cost on fresh tasks. Different objects, both honest in their own domains — same ruling as the chart/dial name collision at edge (e).
